comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter circled the Facebook/Twitter share icons in the file row of the Mixdrop page mxdrop.click, which the AdGuard Social Media filter did not hide. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for those two anchors validated in the reporter's own settings profile:⁠ the icons are gone, no residue, page intact. ## Rule `mxdrop.click##.s-wrapper > .sc` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a social widget (Facebook/Twitter share buttons) and matches the stated purpose of the AdGuard Social Media filter, which blocks social media widgets such as Share buttons on third-party sites; the icons are not part of the site's functionality such as comments or social login. No policy rule in the run instruction closes it:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing page. Site traffic is not a blocking concern for this widely used file-hosting platform family that already has rules in the repository. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/0cbe282a7b179745c082e2d570fc4e9d4b110538/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/43536054833 Automated analysis against filters at `0cbe282`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.
